newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Northern League says won't vote on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Northern League says won't vote on budget.

text.p: Italy's separatist Northern League party said on Monday it would not take part in voting on the 1997 budget bill in the lower house of parliament, following a similar stance by the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance.
The League's decision means the government can still get the budget through parliament providing the hard-left Communist Refoundation party votes with the government and keeps the house quorate.

Domenico Comino, leader of the League in the Chamber of Deputies or lower house, told the government in a speech: "You are not sticking to your electoral programme and so the League will not participate in the vote. Vote for it yourselves."
"This budget is pursuing contrasting and paradoxical objectives which cannot be realised and which defend the status quo of a centralised and dissolute state," Camino said.
The Freedom Alliance said earlier it would not participate on voting for the 1997 budget package which aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) from next year's budget deficit.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has asked parliament to give his government numerous special powers to dictate policy on key budget areas, including tax reform, but the centre-right has rejected the request. The special powers through a delegate law would allow the government a free had to draft legislation within pre-defined limits, in this case on tax reform, without constantly referring back to parliament.
